question: A solid right circular cone is cut into two parts by a plane parallel to its base and at a point one-third vertically below its vertex. What is the ratio of the volume of the smaller cone to that of the whole cone?
solution:
Given:

A solid right circular cone is cut into two parts by a plane parallel to its base and at a point one-third vertically below its vertex.

Concept used:

The volume of a cone = (πR²H ÷ 3) 

R and H are the radius of the base and height of the cone respectively.

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6eb349e472bf015bb11f893641549e0d5aace885cd913a405e4f0c4d53f13fa1.png] 

Let the radius of the base and the height of the solid circular cone be R and H units respectively.

Hence,

The height of the cone that is cut from the original cone = {H over 3} units

The radius of the cone that is cut from the original cone = {R over 3} units

Thus, the required ratio

{π ({R over 3})² {H over 3} over 3} : {π R² H over 3}

⇒ {1 over 81} : {1 over 3} 

⇒ 1 : 27

⇒ {1 over 27}

**∴ {1 over 27} is the ratio of the volume of the smaller cone to that of the whole cone.**
